newsitem.title: USA: Florida Power's Crystal River 3 still shut.
newsitem.headline: Florida Power's Crystal River 3 still shut.

text.p: Florida Power Corp's (FPC) Crystal River 3 nuclear power unit remained shut after tripping off line Monday due to a leak in a lubrication oil line to the unit's turbine shaft, the company said Friday.
The utility still has no date for when the 825 megawatt (MW) station in Red Level, Fla., likely would return to service, said company spokeswoman Melodye Hendrix.
She suggested the unit could resume operation next week, but cautioned, "That's just tentative."
Meanwhile, repair crews were replacing the section of the lube oil line where the leak was discovered, she said.
Crystal River produces 15 percent of the electricity FPC delivers in its Florida service territory. The facility also has four fossil-fueled units, with a combined generating capacity of 2,276 MW.
Florida Power, a subsidiary of Florida Progress Corp, is the operator and majority owner of Crystal River 3. Ten Florida municipal utilities own the remaining interests in the unit.
